text: I know this reply is a little late, but I'm interested. Do you want to capture soundwaves and convert them into electrical waves? Or do you want to use an amplifier to amplify different signals? Regardless which signal you're attempting to amplify, a sound amplifier should work. Sound amps like most type of digital signal amplifications mostly use transistors for the amplification process. You have one control/input wave (any electrical signal works so long as it's within the parameters of that transistor) which controls the frequency, and one output wave, which is the amplified signal. The input wave creates a variable resistance within the transistors, and the output wave is sent through this variable resistance, thus controlling it. The output wave can again be just about anything, so long as the transistor is rated for it. You could do multiple transistors in a row, but that could lead to signal degradation. Most amps have other types of controls, where you can modulate the frequency ranges (low/bass, mid, treble, or even more options in kHz) and signal input/output control. Hope this was of some help!
